material_id:
Hari ketiga belas! Ini hari bos kecil sebelum Hari Review Adaptif. Di Structure kita menyisir **10 kesalahan paling umum** yang hampir selalu muncul di tes. Listening hari ini lebih cepat dan memakai lebih banyak **aksen British**, dan Reading memakai **teks panjang** sekitar 450 kata.

=== listening
## Dialog cepat dan aksen UK
Kecepatan dan aksen sering membuat panik, padahal polanya sama. Ungkapan British seperti *no joy* (tidak berhasil), *up to my eyes* (sibuk sekali), *fancy a…?* (mau…?), dan *on paper* (secara teori) sering muncul. Jawaban pendek seperti *On paper, maybe* biasanya berarti ragu.
Perumpamaan: aksen itu seperti tulisan tangan orang lain. Hurufnya terlihat beda, tetapi kata-katanya sama. Begitu terbiasa, kamu membacanya secepat tulisanmu sendiri.
> Ungkapan British → cari maknanya, bukan kata per kata · jawaban pendek + nada ragu = tidak setuju
✓ Fokus pada kata kerja dan kata kunci, bukan pada aksen
✓ Biarkan satu kata yang terlewat, kejar maknanya
✕ Berhenti mendengarkan karena satu kata terdengar asing
✕ Mengartikan *up to my eyes* secara harfiah

=== structure
## 10 kesalahan paling umum
1. Pelaku dan kata kerja tidak cocok (*The quality of the photos **are***).
2. Setelah *have/has/had* bukan V3 (*has **decide***).
3. Kata sifat dipakai untuk menerangkan kata kerja (*worked **tireless***).
4. Daftar tidak sejajar (*analyze, **writing**, and present*).
5. Pelaku dobel (*My brother, who lives in Surabaya, **he** works*).
6. Kata depan dipakai seperti kata sambung (*Despite / Although*).
7. Kelas kata salah (*the **construct** of the stadium*).
8. Perbandingan salah (*more accurate than*, bukan *accurater*).
9. Pasif dan aktif tertukar (*letters **were sent***).
10. Kata ganti tidak cocok dengan kata benda (*the company … **its***).
Perumpamaan: daftar ini seperti daftar tilang yang paling sering. Kalau kamu hafal pelanggarannya, kamu langsung melihatnya di jalan.
> Pelaku-kata kerja → bentuk kata kerja → kelas kata → paralel → pelaku dobel → kata sambung → perbandingan → aktif/pasif → kata ganti
✓ Cek nomor 1 dan 2 lebih dulu: paling sering keluar
✓ Kalau satu bagian terasa janggal, uji dengan kesepuluh aturan ini
✕ Menganggap kalimat panjang pasti salah
✕ Memilih bagian yang hanya terdengar asing padahal benar

=== reading
## Teks panjang 450 kata
Teks panjang tidak harus dibaca pelan dari awal sampai akhir. Skim kalimat pertama tiap paragraf untuk membuat peta, lalu baca detail hanya saat soal memintanya. Untuk soal main idea, ingat seluruh peta; untuk soal detail, langsung ke paragraf yang tepat.
Perumpamaan: teks panjang itu seperti mal besar. Lihat papan petunjuk lantai dulu, baru masuk ke toko yang kamu butuhkan.
> Skim kalimat pertama → peta paragraf → scanning untuk detail
✓ Tulis satu kata kunci untuk tiap paragraf
✓ Kerjakan soal yang menyebut nomor paragraf lebih dulu
✕ Membaca ulang seluruh teks untuk setiap soal
✕ Memilih jawaban main idea yang hanya cocok untuk satu paragraf
material_en:
Day thirteen! This is the mini boss before the Adaptive Review Day. In Structure we sweep the **10 most common errors** that almost always appear on the test. Listening is faster today with more **British accents**, and Reading uses **long passages** of about 450 words.

=== listening
## Fast dialogues and UK accents
Speed and accents can cause panic, but the patterns are the same. British phrases such as *no joy* (no success), *up to my eyes* (very busy), *fancy a…?* (would you like…?), and *on paper* (in theory) come up often. Short replies like *On paper, maybe* usually signal doubt.
Analogy: an accent is like someone else's handwriting. The letters look different, but the words are the same. Once you're used to it, you read it as fast as your own.
> British phrase → find the meaning, not each word · short reply + doubtful tone = disagreement
✓ Focus on verbs and keywords, not the accent
✓ Let one missed word go and chase the meaning
✕ Tuning out because one word sounds unfamiliar
✕ Taking *up to my eyes* literally

=== structure
## The 10 most common errors
1. Subject and verb don't agree (*The quality of the photos **are***).
2. No V3 after *have/has/had* (*has **decide***).
3. An adjective describing a verb (*worked **tireless***).
4. A list that isn't parallel (*analyze, **writing**, and present*).
5. A double subject (*My brother, who lives in Surabaya, **he** works*).
6. A preposition used like a conjunction (*Despite / Although*).
7. The wrong word class (*the **construct** of the stadium*).
8. A wrong comparison (*more accurate than*, not *accurater*).
9. Active and passive mixed up (*letters **were sent***).
10. A pronoun that doesn't match its noun (*the company … **its***).
Analogy: this list is like the most common traffic tickets. Know the violations and you'll spot them on the road immediately.
> Subject-verb → verb form → word class → parallelism → double subject → connector → comparison → active/passive → pronoun
✓ Check numbers 1 and 2 first: they appear most often
✓ If a part feels odd, test it against these ten rules
✕ Assuming a long sentence must be wrong
✕ Picking a part that only sounds unfamiliar but is correct

=== reading
## Long passages of 450 words
A long passage doesn't have to be read slowly from start to finish. Skim the first sentence of each paragraph to build a map, then read details only when a question asks for them. For main idea questions, remember the whole map; for detail questions, go straight to the right paragraph.
Analogy: a long passage is like a big shopping mall. Check the floor directory first, then walk into the shop you need.
> Skim first sentences → paragraph map → scan for details
✓ Write one keyword per paragraph
✓ Answer questions that name a paragraph first
✕ Rereading the whole passage for each question
✕ Picking a main idea that fits only one paragraph

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Did you manage to get hold of Professor Grant about the extension?

script.speaker: W2
script.text: I rang his office three times this morning, but no joy.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: She was not able to reach the professor.
She was able to speak with the professor.
She enjoyed talking with the professor.
She will visit the professor's office tomorrow.
questions.key_sentence: I rang his office three times this morning, but no joy.
questions.key_translation_id: Aku telepon kantornya tiga kali tadi pagi, tapi nggak nyambung juga.
questions.why_correct_id: **rang** itu bahasa British buat nelepon. **no joy** itu ungkapan British yang artinya nggak berhasil. Jadi dia nelepon tiga kali tapi nggak berhasil ngehubungin profesornya.
questions.why_correct_en: **rang** is British for phoned. **no joy** is a British phrase for no success. She called three times but couldn't reach him.

why_wrong_id.1: Kebalikannya. **no joy** artinya gagal.
why_wrong_id.2: Ini arti harfiah **joy**, senang. Ungkapan ini nggak ngomongin perasaan.
why_wrong_id.3: Rencana datang ke kantor besok nggak disebut.

why_wrong_en.1: The opposite. **no joy** means she failed.
why_wrong_en.2: That's the literal **joy**. The phrase isn't about feelings.
why_wrong_en.3: No visit tomorrow is mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: **No joy** itu kayak mancing seharian terus pulang dengan ember kosong. Usaha ada, hasil nihil.
questions.analogy_en: **No joy** is a whole day of fishing and an empty bucket. Effort, no catch.
questions.tip_id: Ungkapan British pendek kayak **no joy** atau **cheers** sering jadi kunci. Artiin maknanya, bukan katanya.
questions.tip_en: Short British phrases like **no joy** or **cheers** are often the key. Translate the meaning, not the words.
questions.liaison_note: **but no joy** kedengeran nyambung jadi bət-nəʊ-dʒɔɪ dengan aksen British.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Fancy a coffee before the seminar?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: I'd love one, but I'm up to my eyes in marking this week.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply?
options: He already had coffee this morning.
He will mark her paper during the seminar.
He is too busy to join her.
questions.key_sentence: I'd love one, but I'm up to my eyes in marking this week.
questions.key_translation_id: Pengen banget, tapi aku lagi sibuk banget ngoreksi tugas minggu ini.
questions.why_correct_id: **I'd love one, but…** itu penolakan halus. **up to my eyes** itu ungkapan British buat sibuk banget, kerjaan numpuk sampai mata. **marking** artinya ngoreksi tugas. Jadi dia terlalu sibuk buat ikut ngopi.
questions.why_correct_en: **I'd love one, but…** is a polite no. **up to my eyes** means extremely busy. **marking** is grading. He's too busy to join her.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah **eyes**. Matanya baik-baik aja.
why_wrong_id.1: Kopi tadi pagi nggak disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Dia ngoreksi tugas mahasiswanya, dan nggak disebut bakal dikerjain pas seminar.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal **eyes**. His eyes are fine.
why_wrong_en.1: Morning coffee isn't mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: He's grading student work, and nothing says during the seminar.

questions.analogy_id: **Up to my eyes** itu kayak tenggelam dalam tumpukan kertas sampai cuma matanya yang kelihatan.
questions.analogy_en: **Up to my eyes** is being buried in papers until only your eyes show.
questions.tip_id: **I'd love to, but…** atau **I'd love one, but…** hampir selalu artinya nggak. Alasannya ada setelah **but**.
questions.tip_en: **I'd love to, but…** or **I'd love one, but…** almost always means no. The reason follows **but**.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: The new bus timetable looks much better, doesn't it?

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply?
options: She doubts that the timetable will work well in practice.
She prefers reading the timetable on paper.
She agrees that the timetable is much better.
She has not seen the new timetable.
questions.why_correct_id: **On paper** artinya secara teori atau kelihatannya. Ditambah **maybe**, jawaban pendek ini nunjukin dia ragu. Kesannya bagus di jadwal, tapi belum tentu jalan di kenyataan.
questions.why_correct_en: **On paper** means in theory. With **maybe**, the short reply shows doubt: good on the schedule, not necessarily in reality.

why_wrong_id.1: Ini arti harfiah **on paper**, kertas. Ungkapan ini soal teori dan kenyataan.
why_wrong_id.2: Kebalikannya. **maybe** nunjukin dia nggak setuju penuh.
why_wrong_id.3: Dia jelas udah lihat, buktinya dia ngasih penilaian.

why_wrong_en.1: That's the literal **paper**. The phrase is about theory versus reality.
why_wrong_en.2: The opposite. **maybe** shows she doesn't fully agree.
why_wrong_en.3: She clearly saw it, since she judges it.

questions.analogy_id: **On paper, maybe** itu kayak lihat foto makanan di menu. Kelihatannya enak, tapi rasanya belum tentu sama.
questions.analogy_en: **On paper, maybe** is a food photo on a menu. It looks great, but the taste may differ.
questions.tip_id: Jawaban pendek plus **maybe** atau **I suppose** biasanya artinya ragu, bukan setuju.
questions.tip_en: A short reply with **maybe** or **I suppose** usually means doubt, not agreement.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Shall we take the bus to the museum?

script.speaker: M1
script.text: It's only ten minutes on foot, and the weather's lovely.

questions.prompt: What does the man suggest?
questions.key_sentence: It's only ten minutes on foot, and the weather's lovely.
questions.key_translation_id: Cuma sepuluh menit jalan kaki, dan cuacanya lagi enak.
questions.why_correct_id: Dia nggak bilang langsung ayo jalan, tapi ngasih dua alasan: **only ten minutes on foot** dan **the weather's lovely**. Dua alasan itu nyiratin saran buat jalan kaki ke museum.
questions.why_correct_en: He doesn't say walk directly, but gives two reasons: **only ten minutes on foot** and **the weather's lovely**. Together they suggest walking.

why_wrong_id.0: Bus berikutnya nggak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.1: Taksi nggak disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Dia malah ngasih alasan buat pergi sekarang.

why_wrong_en.0: A later bus isn't discussed.
why_wrong_en.1: Taxis aren't mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: He gives reasons to go now.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak teman yang bilang mejanya cuma di seberang, kenapa harus pesan antar. Dia nggak bilang jalan, tapi maksudnya jelas.
questions.analogy_en: Like a friend saying the place is just across the street. No direct suggestion, but the meaning is clear.
questions.tip_id: Saran nggak selalu pakai **Let's**. Kadang cuma berupa alasan yang ngarah ke satu pilihan.
questions.tip_en: Suggestions don't always use **Let's**. Sometimes they're just reasons pointing to one choice.
questions.liaison_note: **weather's lovely** kedengeran kayak wedha-zlavli dengan aksen British.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: You look worried. Is everything all right with your dissertation?

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Not really. My supervisor's going on research leave next month, so I'll need someone new to read my drafts.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Have you asked Dr. Okafor? She works on urban planning too.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: I thought about it, but she's already supervising eight students. I doubt she'd have time for me.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: You'd be surprised. She told our seminar group she's taking on two more this term.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Really? Then I'll email her tonight. The only problem is that my first chapter isn't finished.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: I wouldn't worry. Send her your outline and the introduction. That's usually enough to start a conversation.

questions.prompt: What is the man's main problem?
options: He needs a new dissertation supervisor.
He cannot find a seminar to join.
He has too many students to supervise.
questions.key_sentence: My supervisor's going on research leave next month, so I'll need someone new to read my drafts.
questions.key_translation_id: Pembimbingku cuti riset bulan depan, jadi aku butuh orang baru buat baca drafku.
questions.why_correct_id: Si pria bilang pembimbingnya cuti riset, jadi dia **need someone new to read my drafts**. Masalah utamanya nyari pembimbing skripsi baru.
questions.why_correct_en: His supervisor is going on leave, so he needs **someone new to read my drafts**. His problem is finding a new supervisor.

why_wrong_id.0: Bab pertamanya belum kelar, bukan gagal.
why_wrong_id.2: Seminar cuma tempat si wanita dengar info soal Dr. Okafor.
why_wrong_id.3: Yang ngebimbing delapan mahasiswa itu Dr. Okafor, bukan dia.

why_wrong_en.0: His first chapter isn't finished, not failed.
why_wrong_en.2: The seminar is just where she heard about Dr. Okafor.
why_wrong_en.3: Dr. Okafor supervises eight students, not him.

questions.analogy_id: Masalah utama itu kayak keluhan pasien di awal. Sisa obrolan cuma cari obatnya.
questions.analogy_en: The main problem is the patient's opening complaint. The rest is finding the cure.
questions.tip_id: Soal masalah utama? Cari kalimat yang pakai **so I'll need** atau **the problem is** di awal obrolan.
questions.tip_en: Main problem? Look for **so I'll need** or **the problem is** early in the talk.

questions.prompt: Why was the man unsure about asking Dr. Okafor?
options: She works in a different field.
He did not like her seminar.
She is also going on research leave.
He thought she was too busy.
questions.key_sentence: I thought about it, but she's already supervising eight students. I doubt she'd have time for me.
questions.key_translation_id: Aku udah kepikiran, tapi beliau udah ngebimbing delapan mahasiswa. Kayaknya nggak sempat.
questions.why_correct_id: Dia bilang Dr. Okafor **already supervising eight students**, dan **I doubt she'd have time for me**. Jadi dia ngira dosennya terlalu sibuk.
questions.why_correct_en: He says Dr. Okafor is **already supervising eight students** and **I doubt she'd have time for me**. He thought she was too busy.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Dr. Okafor juga di bidang tata kota.
why_wrong_id.1: Dia nggak ngomongin suka atau nggak sama seminarnya.
why_wrong_id.2: Yang cuti riset itu pembimbing lamanya, bukan Dr. Okafor.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. Dr. Okafor also works on urban planning.
why_wrong_en.1: He says nothing about liking her seminar.
why_wrong_en.2: His old supervisor is going on leave, not Dr. Okafor.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak nggak berani minta tolong teman yang kelihatannya super sibuk, padahal dia lagi buka slot.
questions.analogy_en: Like hesitating to ask a busy-looking friend who actually has free slots.
questions.tip_id: **I doubt…** plus alasan sebelumnya? Itu jawaban soal **why unsure**.
questions.tip_en: **I doubt…** plus the reason before it answers **why unsure**.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Dr. Okafor?
options: She only supervises students in their final year.
She is willing to supervise more students.
She has already read the man's outline.
She will leave the university next month.
questions.key_sentence: You'd be surprised. She told our seminar group she's taking on two more this term.
questions.key_translation_id: Kamu bakal kaget. Beliau bilang ke kelompok seminar kami kalau semester ini mau nerima dua lagi.
questions.why_correct_id: Si wanita bilang Dr. Okafor **taking on two more this term**, mau nerima dua mahasiswa lagi semester ini. Artinya beliau masih mau dan masih bisa ngebimbing lebih banyak mahasiswa.
questions.why_correct_en: She says Dr. Okafor is **taking on two more this term**. So she's willing to supervise more students.

why_wrong_id.0: Syarat tahun terakhir nggak disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Si pria baru mau ngirim email malam ini. Kerangkanya belum dikirim.
why_wrong_id.3: Yang pergi itu pembimbing lama si pria, cuti riset, bukan Dr. Okafor.

why_wrong_en.0: No final-year rule is mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: He'll email tonight. Nothing has been sent.
why_wrong_en.3: His old supervisor is leaving on research leave, not Dr. Okafor.

questions.analogy_id: **taking on two more** itu kayak restoran yang bilang masih ada dua meja kosong. Artinya masih nerima tamu.
questions.analogy_en: **taking on two more** is a restaurant saying it has two free tables. It's still taking guests.
questions.tip_id: **You'd be surprised** biasanya nandain info yang ngebantah dugaan orang sebelumnya. Inferensinya ada di situ.
questions.tip_en: **You'd be surprised** usually introduces info that overturns the earlier assumption. The inference sits there.

script.speaker: LEC
script.text: In the hot summer of 1858, the River Thames in London smelled so terrible that newspapers called it the Great Stink. For centuries, the city's waste had flowed straight into the river, and the population had grown far faster than anyone had planned for. At the time, most experts believed that diseases such as cholera spread through bad air. That belief was wrong. We now know cholera spreads mainly through contaminated water. But the smell was so strong that even members of Parliament, whose building stands beside the river, demanded action. The engineer Joseph Bazalgette was asked to design a solution. His plan was a network of large sewers that would catch waste before it reached the central river and carry it far to the east, away from the city. The main system was largely finished in the 1870s. One detail is often mentioned: Bazalgette made many of the pipes about twice as wide as his calculations required, because he expected London to keep growing. That decision is one reason parts of the system still work today. So even though the original theory about disease was mistaken, the response to it saved many lives.

questions.prompt: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: How London solved a sewage crisis in the 1800s
Why newspapers in London became popular
The history of the British Parliament building
questions.key_sentence: In the hot summer of 1858, the River Thames in London smelled so terrible that newspapers called it the Great Stink.
questions.key_translation_id: Di musim panas yang panas tahun 1858, Sungai Thames di London baunya parah banget sampai koran nyebutnya the Great Stink.
questions.why_correct_id: Kuliahnya dibuka pakai masalah bau busuk Sungai Thames tahun 1858, terus ngejelasin solusinya: jaringan saluran pembuangan rancangan Bazalgette. Jadi topiknya cara London ngatasin krisis limbah di abad ke-19.
questions.why_correct_en: It opens with the Thames stench of 1858 and explains the fix: Bazalgette's sewer network. So it's how London solved a sewage crisis in the 1800s.

why_wrong_id.1: Koran cuma yang ngasih julukan Great Stink.
why_wrong_id.2: Kolera dibahas soal cara penyebarannya, bukan penemuannya.
why_wrong_id.3: Gedung Parlemen cuma disebut karena letaknya di tepi sungai.

why_wrong_en.1: Newspapers only gave the Great Stink its name.
why_wrong_en.2: Cholera comes up for how it spreads, not its discovery.
why_wrong_en.3: Parliament appears only because it sits by the river.

questions.analogy_id: Lecture yang dibuka pakai krisis itu kayak film bencana. Judulnya biasanya soal cara selamat dari bencananya.
questions.analogy_en: A lecture that opens with a crisis is a disaster film. The title is usually about surviving it.
questions.tip_id: Lecture sejarah sering berpola masalah lalu solusi. Pilih topik yang nyakup dua-duanya.
questions.tip_en: History lectures often go problem then solution. Pick the topic that covers both.

questions.prompt: According to the professor, why did Bazalgette make many pipes wider than necessary?
options: Wider pipes were cheaper to build.
He expected London's population to keep growing.
The river water needed more space during floods.
questions.key_sentence: Bazalgette made many of the pipes about twice as wide as his calculations required, because he expected London to keep growing.
questions.key_translation_id: Bazalgette bikin banyak pipa kira-kira dua kali lebih lebar dari hitungannya, karena dia ngira London bakal terus tumbuh.
questions.why_correct_id: Alasannya disebut pakai **because**: **he expected London to keep growing**. Dia ngira kotanya bakal terus berkembang, jadi pipanya dibikin dua kali lebih lebar.
questions.why_correct_en: The reason follows **because**: **he expected London to keep growing**.

why_wrong_id.0: Biaya pipa nggak disebut.
why_wrong_id.1: Parlemen cuma nuntut tindakan, bukan ukuran pipa.
why_wrong_id.3: Banjir sungai nggak dibahas.

why_wrong_en.0: Pipe cost isn't mentioned.
why_wrong_en.1: Parliament only demanded action, not pipe sizes.
why_wrong_en.3: River floods aren't discussed.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak beli sepatu anak satu nomor lebih gede karena kakinya masih tumbuh.
questions.analogy_en: Like buying a child's shoes a size up because their feet are still growing.
questions.tip_id: **One detail is often mentioned** nandain info yang sering ditanya. Pasang telinga di kalimat sesudahnya.
questions.tip_en: **One detail is often mentioned** flags a likely question. Listen to the next sentence.

questions.prompt: What does the professor imply about the belief that disease spread through bad air?
options: It was correct and led to the sewer system.
It was proven true by Parliament.
It was wrong, but it still led to a useful solution.
questions.key_sentence: So even though the original theory about disease was mistaken, the response to it saved many lives.
questions.key_translation_id: Jadi walaupun teori awal soal penyakit itu keliru, tindakan yang diambil karenanya justru nyelametin banyak nyawa.
questions.why_correct_id: Dosennya bilang **That belief was wrong**. Tapi di akhir dia nambahin: walaupun teorinya keliru, **the response to it saved many lives**. Jadi teorinya salah, tapi tetap ngehasilin solusi yang berguna.
questions.why_correct_en: The professor says **That belief was wrong**, then ends: though the theory was mistaken, **the response to it saved many lives**.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Dosennya bilang keyakinan itu salah.
why_wrong_id.1: Parlemen nggak ngebuktiin apa pun. Mereka cuma nuntut tindakan karena baunya.
why_wrong_id.3: Penyebab Great Stink itu limbah di sungai, bukan keyakinan soal udara.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. The professor calls the belief wrong.
why_wrong_en.1: Parliament proved nothing. It only demanded action over the smell.
why_wrong_en.3: The Great Stink came from waste in the river, not from a belief.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak orang yang rajin cuci tangan karena takut hantu kuman. Alasannya keliru, tapi kebiasaannya tetap bikin sehat.
questions.analogy_en: Like someone who washes their hands to scare off imaginary germ ghosts. Wrong reason, healthy habit.
questions.tip_id: Kalimat penutup yang pakai **even though** sering nyimpen pesan utama dosen. Soal **imply** suka ngambil dari situ.
questions.tip_en: A closing line with **even though** often holds the lecturer's key point. **Imply** questions love it.

items.prompt: The ______ of the new stadium took nearly three years.
items.why_correct_id: **The ___ of the new stadium** itu pelaku kalimat, jadi butuh kata benda. Kata bendanya pakai akhiran -tion: **construction**.
items.why_correct_en: **The ___ of the new stadium** is the subject, so it needs a noun: **construction**.

why_wrong_id.0: **construct** itu kata kerja.
why_wrong_id.1: **constructive** itu kata sifat, artinya membangun dalam arti positif.
why_wrong_id.2: **constructed** itu V2/V3, bukan kata benda.

why_wrong_en.0: **construct** is a verb.
why_wrong_en.1: **constructive** is an adjective, meaning helpful.
why_wrong_en.2: **constructed** is V2/V3, not a noun.

items.analogy_id: Pola **The ___ of** itu kayak bingkai foto. Cuma muat benda, bukan aksi.
items.analogy_en: **The ___ of** is a picture frame. It only fits a thing, not an action.
items.tip_en: **The + ___ + of**? Look for a noun ending: -tion, -ment, -ance, -ity.

items.prompt: ______ the long delay, the passengers remained calm and patient.
items.why_correct_id: Setelah rumpang cuma ada frasa benda: **the long delay**. Kata benda butuh kata depan. Maknanya kontras: telat lama tapi tetap tenang. Jadi **Despite**.
items.why_correct_en: Only a noun phrase follows: **the long delay**. A noun needs a preposition, and the meaning is contrast: **Despite**.

why_wrong_id.0: **Although** itu kata sambung. Butuh pelaku plus kata kerja.
why_wrong_id.1: **Because** juga kata sambung, dan artinya karena. Maknanya nggak cocok.
why_wrong_id.3: **However** itu penghubung antarkalimat, nggak bisa langsung diikutin frasa benda kayak gini.

why_wrong_en.0: **Although** is a conjunction. It needs a subject and verb.
why_wrong_en.1: **Because** is a conjunction meaning since. The meaning doesn't fit.
why_wrong_en.3: **However** links sentences and can't take a noun phrase like this.

items.analogy_id: **Despite** itu troli kecil, cukup bawa satu barang: **the long delay**.
items.analogy_en: **Despite** is a small trolley carrying one item: **the long delay**.
items.tip_id: Cek dulu yang ada setelah rumpang. Cuma kata benda? Pilih **despite** atau **in spite of**.
items.tip_en: Check what follows. Just a noun? Pick **despite** or **in spite of**.

items.prompt: The second experiment produced results that were ______ than those of the first.
items.why_correct_id: Ada **than**, jadi butuh comparative. **accurate** itu kata panjang, jadi pakai **more**: **more accurate**.
items.why_correct_en: **than** calls for a comparative. **accurate** is long, so: **more accurate**.

why_wrong_id.0: Kata panjang nggak pakai -er. **accurater** nggak ada.
why_wrong_id.1: **most accurate** itu superlative, pasangannya **the**, bukan **than**.
why_wrong_id.2: **the more accurate** cuma dipakai di pola khusus kayak **the more …, the more …**.

why_wrong_en.0: Long words don't take -er. **accurater** doesn't exist.
why_wrong_en.1: **most accurate** is a superlative. It pairs with **the**, not **than**.
why_wrong_en.2: **the more accurate** only appears in patterns like **the more …, the more …**.

items.analogy_id: Kata panjang pakai jas **more**. Jaket -er cuma muat buat kata pendek.
items.analogy_en: Long words wear the **more** coat. The -er jacket only fits short words.
items.tip_id: **than** di kalimat? Cari **-er** atau **more**. Hitung suku katanya.
items.tip_en: **than** in the sentence? Look for **-er** or **more**. Count the syllables.

items.prompt: Thousands of letters ______ to the radio station after the interview was broadcast.
items.why_correct_id: Surat nggak bisa ngirim dirinya sendiri. Surat dikirim orang, jadi butuh pasif. Kejadiannya lampau, **after the interview was broadcast**. Jadi **were sent**.
items.why_correct_en: Letters can't send themselves; people send them. So it's passive, and past: **were sent**.

why_wrong_id.1: **sent** sendirian bikin kalimat aktif: surat yang ngirim sesuatu, tapi nggak ada objeknya.
why_wrong_id.2: **were sending** itu aktif continuous. Suratnya jadi pelaku yang lagi ngirim.
why_wrong_id.3: **have sent** juga aktif, dan nggak cocok sama urutan waktu lampau di kalimat ini.

why_wrong_en.1: **sent** alone makes it active: the letters would send something, with no object.
why_wrong_en.2: **were sending** is active: the letters would be doing the sending.
why_wrong_en.3: **have sent** is active and doesn't fit the past sequence here.

items.analogy_id: Surat itu penumpang, bukan sopir. Penumpang naik mobil pasif: **were sent**.
items.analogy_en: Letters are passengers, not drivers. Passengers ride in the passive: **were sent**.
items.tip_id: Tanya dulu: pelakunya bisa ngelakuin aksi itu sendiri? Kalau nggak, pakai be + V3.
items.tip_en: Ask first: can the subject do the action? If not, use be + V3.

items.prompt: The quality of the {A}photographs{/A} in these old books {B}are{/B} {C}surprisingly{/C} {D}high{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Pelaku aslinya **The quality**, tunggal. **of the photographs in these old books** cuma keterangan panjang. Jadi **are** harus jadi **is**.
items.why_correct_en: The real subject is **The quality**, singular. The long **of** phrase is just a description. So **are** should be **is**.

why_wrong_id.0: **photographs** jamak pas setelah **of the**.
why_wrong_id.2: **surprisingly** itu adverb yang nerangin kata sifat **high**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **high** itu kata sifat yang pas setelah **is**.

why_wrong_en.0: Plural **photographs** fits after **of the**.
why_wrong_en.2: **surprisingly** modifies the adjective **high**. Fine.
why_wrong_en.3: **high** is a fine adjective after **is**.

items.analogy_id: Frasa **of** yang panjang itu kayak gerbong tambahan. Sepanjang apa pun, lokomotifnya tetap **quality**.
items.analogy_en: A long **of** phrase is extra carriages. However long, the engine is still **quality**.
items.tip_id: Ini kesalahan nomor 1 di tes. Coret frasa **of …**, terus cocokin kata kerjanya.
items.tip_en: This is error number 1 on the test. Cross out **of …** and match the verb.

items.prompt: The committee {A}has{/A} {B}decide{/B} to {C}postpone{/C} the {D}meeting{/D} until next month.
items.why_correct_id: Habis **has** harus V3. **decide** masih V1. Jadi **decide** harus jadi **decided**.
items.why_correct_en: **has** needs V3. **decide** is still V1. It should be **decided**.

why_wrong_id.0: **has** tunggal, cocok sama **The committee**.
why_wrong_id.2: **to postpone** itu infinitive yang pas setelah **decided**.
why_wrong_id.3: **the meeting** itu objek yang aman.

why_wrong_en.0: **has** is singular, matching **The committee**.
why_wrong_en.2: **to postpone** fits after **decided**.
why_wrong_en.3: **the meeting** is a fine object.

items.analogy_id: **Has** itu kernet bus jurusan V3. **decide** masih pakai seragam V1, jadi nggak boleh naik.
items.analogy_en: **Has** is the V3 bus conductor. **decide** is still in V1 uniform, so no boarding.
items.tip_id: Kesalahan nomor 2: tiap ketemu **have**, **has**, **had**, lirik kata kerja sesudahnya.
items.tip_en: Error number 2: every **have**, **has**, **had**, check the next verb.

items.prompt: The volunteers worked {A}tireless{/A} {B}to repair{/B} the homes {C}damaged{/C} by the {D}flood{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: **tireless** nerangin cara relawan bekerja, alias nerangin kata kerja **worked**. Yang nerangin kata kerja itu adverb. Jadi **tireless** harus jadi **tirelessly**.
items.why_correct_en: **tireless** describes how they worked, so it modifies **worked**. That needs **tirelessly**.

why_wrong_id.1: **to repair** itu infinitive tujuan yang aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **damaged** itu reduced clause pasif yang pas: bangunan yang dirusak banjir.
why_wrong_id.3: **the flood** itu kata benda yang pas setelah **by**.

why_wrong_en.1: **to repair** is a fine purpose infinitive.
why_wrong_en.2: **damaged** is a fine reduced passive: homes damaged by the flood.
why_wrong_en.3: **the flood** fits after **by**.

items.analogy_id: Kata sifat itu cat, adverb itu gaya nyetir. Cara kerja butuh gaya nyetir: **tirelessly**.
items.analogy_en: An adjective is paint, an adverb is driving style. How they worked needs **tirelessly**.
items.tip_id: Kesalahan nomor 3: kata kerja aksi plus kata yang jawab gimana? Biasanya butuh -ly.
items.tip_en: Error number 3: an action verb plus a how word? It usually needs -ly.

items.prompt: The course teaches students how to {A}analyze{/A} data, {B}writing{/B} clear reports, and {C}present{/C} their {D}findings{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Daftar setelah **how to** harus sejajar: **analyze**, ___, **present**, semuanya V1. **writing** itu V-ing, jadi nggak sejajar. Harusnya **write**.
items.why_correct_en: The list after **how to** must be parallel: **analyze**, ___, **present**, all V1. **writing** breaks it. It should be **write**.

why_wrong_id.0: **analyze** itu V1 yang pas setelah **how to**.
why_wrong_id.2: **present** itu V1 yang sejajar sama **analyze**.
why_wrong_id.3: **findings** itu kata benda jamak yang pas.

why_wrong_en.0: **analyze** is a fine V1 after **how to**.
why_wrong_en.2: **present** is parallel with **analyze**.
why_wrong_en.3: **findings** is a fine plural noun.

items.analogy_id: Tiga gerbong yang ditarik **how to** harus seukuran. **writing** itu gerbong yang ukurannya beda sendiri.
items.analogy_en: Three carriages pulled by **how to** must match. **writing** is the odd-sized one.
items.tip_id: Kesalahan nomor 4: daftar **X, Y, and Z**? Samain bentuk Y sama X dan Z.
items.tip_en: Error number 4: a list **X, Y, and Z**? Make Y match X and Z.

items.prompt: My older {A}brother{/A}, who {B}lives{/B} in Surabaya, {C}he{/C} works as a {D}nurse{/D} at a large hospital.
items.why_correct_id: Pelakunya **My older brother**, terus ada penjelas di antara koma, **who lives in Surabaya**. Habis itu muncul **he** lagi. Nah, ini biang keroknya: pelakunya jadi dobel. Hapus **he**.
items.why_correct_en: The subject is **My older brother**, followed by a comma clause, **who lives in Surabaya**. Then **he** appears again. That's a double subject. Drop **he**.

why_wrong_id.0: **brother** itu kata benda yang pas jadi pelaku.
why_wrong_id.1: **lives** tunggal, cocok sama **who**, yang nunjuk ke **brother**.
why_wrong_id.3: **a nurse** itu kata benda yang pas setelah **as**.

why_wrong_en.0: **brother** is a fine subject noun.
why_wrong_en.1: **lives** is singular, matching **who**, meaning **brother**.
why_wrong_en.3: **a nurse** fits after **as**.

items.analogy_id: Penjelas di antara koma itu kayak iklan di tengah video. Habis iklannya, videonya lanjut tanpa ngulang judul.
items.analogy_en: A comma clause is an ad in the middle of a video. After the ad, the video continues without repeating the title.
items.tip_id: Kesalahan nomor 5: penjelas panjang di antara koma sering bikin penulis nambahin **he** atau **it** lagi. Coret penjelasnya, terus cek.
items.tip_en: Error number 5: long comma clauses tempt writers to add **he** or **it** again. Cross out the clause and check.

items.prompt: The company announced that {A}it{/A} would {B}expand{/B} {C}their{/C} {D}operations{/D} next year.
items.why_correct_id: **their** nunjuk ke **The company**, satu perusahaan, tunggal. Di awal kalimat juga udah dipakai **it**. Kata ganti kepemilikannya harus konsisten dan tunggal: **its**.
items.why_correct_en: **their** refers to **The company**, a single company. The sentence already uses **it**. The possessive must match: **its**.

why_wrong_id.0: **it** pas buat satu perusahaan.
why_wrong_id.1: **expand** itu V1 yang pas setelah **would**.
why_wrong_id.3: **operations** itu kata benda jamak yang aman.

why_wrong_en.0: **it** fits one company.
why_wrong_en.1: **expand** is the right V1 after **would**.
why_wrong_en.3: **operations** is a fine plural noun.

items.analogy_id: Kalau di awal udah manggil perusahaan pakai **it**, terus tiba-tiba ganti jadi **their**, itu kayak ganti nama panggilan teman di tengah obrolan. Bikin bingung.
items.analogy_en: Calling the company **it** and then switching to **their** is like changing a friend's nickname mid-chat. Confusing.
items.tip_id: Kesalahan nomor 10: cek kata ganti sama kata benda yang ditunjuknya. Satu perusahaan, satu tim, satu negara pakai **it** dan **its**.
items.tip_en: Error number 10: match pronouns to their nouns. One company, team, or country takes **it** and **its**.

items.title: How Long Does a Habit Take?
items.body:
Many popular books claim that it takes exactly twenty-one days to form a new habit. The number sounds precise and encouraging, and it appears in countless articles and advertisements. Yet researchers who have studied habits closely tell a more complicated story. The time needed varies widely from person to person and from one behavior to another.

In one well-known study, published in 2009, psychologists asked about a hundred volunteers to choose a new daily behavior, such as drinking a glass of water after breakfast or going for a short run before dinner. Each day, the volunteers reported whether they had performed the behavior and how automatic it felt. The researchers then measured how long it took for the behavior to reach a stable level of automaticity, the point at which it no longer required much conscious effort.

On average, this took about sixty-six days, roughly three times longer than the popular claim. The range was enormous, however. For some volunteers, a simple behavior became automatic in less than three weeks; for others, the estimate stretched to more than eight months. Not surprisingly, easy behaviors such as drinking water became automatic sooner than demanding ones such as daily exercise.

The study also produced a reassuring result. Missing a single day did not seriously damage the process. Volunteers who skipped the behavior occasionally still built the habit, as long as they returned to it the next day. This suggests that perfection is not required; consistency over time matters more than an unbroken record.

Other research helps explain why some habits form faster than others. Behaviors tied to a clear cue, a specific time, place, or preceding action, tend to become automatic more quickly. A plan such as I will stretch for five minutes after I brush my teeth links the new behavior to an existing routine, so the old habit acts as a reminder for the new one.

For learners preparing for a test, the lesson is practical. Instead of expecting a new study routine to feel natural after three weeks, it may be wiser to expect two months or more, and to attach the routine to something already fixed in the day. Progress may feel slow at first, but the effort required usually shrinks as the behavior becomes automatic.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Drinking water after breakfast is the easiest habit to build.
Forming a habit usually takes longer and varies more than the popular twenty-one-day claim suggests.
Most popular books about habits are written by psychologists.
Missing one day makes it impossible to form a habit.
questions.evidence_quote: Yet researchers who have studied habits closely tell a more complicated story. The time needed varies widely from person to person and from one behavior to another.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 1 ngebantah klaim 21 hari: waktunya beda-beda tiap orang dan tiap kebiasaan. Paragraf berikutnya ngasih bukti (rata-rata 66 hari, rentangnya lebar), penjelasan, dan pelajarannya. Jadi ide pokoknya: bentuk kebiasaan biasanya lebih lama dan lebih bervariasi dari klaim populer.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 1 challenges the 21-day claim. Later paragraphs give evidence (66 days on average, a wide range), explanations, and the lesson. So habits usually take longer and vary more than the claim suggests.

why_wrong_id.0: Minum air cuma contoh kebiasaan gampang di paragraf 3. Kesempitan.
why_wrong_id.2: Teks nggak bilang buku-buku populer ditulis psikolog.
why_wrong_id.3: Kebalikannya. Paragraf 4 bilang bolong sehari nggak ngerusak prosesnya.

why_wrong_en.0: Drinking water is one easy example in paragraph 3. Too narrow.
why_wrong_en.2: Nothing says psychologists wrote the popular books.
why_wrong_en.3: The opposite. Paragraph 4 says missing a day doesn't ruin it.

questions.analogy_id: Teks yang dibuka pakai klaim populer terus ditambah **Yet** itu kayak acara bongkar mitos. Main idea-nya ada di bantahannya.
questions.analogy_en: A passage that opens with a popular claim then says **Yet** is a myth-busting show. The main idea is the correction.
questions.tip_id: Lihat **Yet** atau **However** setelah klaim populer di paragraf 1? Ide pokok biasanya ada di kalimat sesudahnya.
questions.tip_en: **Yet** or **However** after a popular claim in paragraph 1? The main idea usually follows.

questions.prompt: According to the 2009 study, about how long did it take on average for a behavior to become automatic?
questions.evidence_quote: On average, this took about sixty-six days, roughly three times longer than the popular claim.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 3 bilang **On average, this took about sixty-six days**. Rata-ratanya sekitar 66 hari.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 3 says **On average, this took about sixty-six days**.

why_wrong_id.0: 21 hari itu klaim populer yang dibantah teks.
why_wrong_id.1: Kurang dari tiga minggu itu waktu tercepat buat sebagian orang, bukan rata-rata.
why_wrong_id.3: Lebih dari delapan bulan itu batas atas rentangnya, bukan rata-rata.

why_wrong_en.0: 21 days is the popular claim the text challenges.
why_wrong_en.1: Under three weeks was the fastest for some, not the average.
why_wrong_en.3: Over eight months is the top of the range, not the average.

questions.analogy_id: Rata-rata itu kayak nilai tengah kelas. Ada yang lebih cepat, ada yang lebih lama, tapi soalnya nanya nilai tengahnya.
questions.analogy_en: The average is the class middle. Some faster, some slower, but the question asks for the middle.
questions.tip_id: Soal angka sering nyediain semua angka dari teks sebagai pengecoh. Cocokin kata **average** sama kalimat buktinya.
questions.tip_en: Number questions offer every number in the text as a trap. Match **average** to the evidence.

questions.prompt: The word **automaticity** in paragraph 2 refers to a state in which a behavior
options: is performed only in the morning
no longer needs much conscious effort
questions.evidence_quote: a stable level of automaticity, the point at which it no longer required much conscious effort.
questions.why_correct_id: Teksnya langsung ngasih definisi setelah koma: **the point at which it no longer required much conscious effort**. Jadi **automaticity** itu keadaan saat kebiasaan nggak butuh banyak usaha sadar lagi.
questions.why_correct_en: The text defines it right after the comma: **the point at which it no longer required much conscious effort**.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah otomatis kayak mesin. Teksnya soal kebiasaan manusia.
why_wrong_id.1: Pagi hari nggak disebut sebagai syarat.
why_wrong_id.2: Rencana yang dikaitin ke rutinitas dibahas di paragraf 5 sebagai cara bantu, bukan arti kata ini.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal machine sense. The text is about human habits.
why_wrong_en.1: Mornings aren't a condition.
why_wrong_en.2: A plan linked to a routine appears in paragraph 5 as a help, not the meaning.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak naik motor setelah lancar. Tangan dan kaki gerak sendiri tanpa mikir.
questions.analogy_en: Like riding a motorbike once you're used to it. Your hands and feet move without thinking.
questions.tip_id: Kata sulit diikutin koma plus **the point at which** atau **which means**? Itu definisi gratis.
questions.tip_en: A hard word followed by a comma and **the point at which** or **which means**? Free definition.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about a student who misses one day of a new study routine?
options: The student must start counting the days again from zero.
The student can still form the habit by continuing the next day.
The student will need exactly twenty-one more days.
The student should stop the routine for a week.
questions.evidence_quote: Volunteers who skipped the behavior occasionally still built the habit, as long as they returned to it the next day.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 4 bilang relawan yang kadang bolong tetap ngebangun kebiasaannya, **as long as they returned to it the next day**. Jadi mahasiswa yang bolong sehari masih bisa ngebangun kebiasaan asal lanjut besoknya.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 4: those who skipped occasionally still built the habit **as long as they returned to it the next day**. So a student who misses a day can still form it.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Teks bilang bolong sehari nggak ngerusak proses.
why_wrong_id.2: 21 hari itu klaim populer yang dibantah. Nggak ada aturan tambahan 21 hari.
why_wrong_id.3: Teks nggak nyaranin berhenti seminggu. Malah sebaiknya lanjut besoknya.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. One missed day doesn't ruin it.
why_wrong_en.2: 21 days is the claim the text rejects.
why_wrong_en.3: No week-long break is suggested. Continue the next day.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak streak di aplikasi belajar yang nggak langsung reset kalau bolong sehari. Yang penting balik lagi besoknya.
questions.analogy_en: Like a learning app streak that doesn't reset after one missed day. Just come back tomorrow.
questions.tip_id: **as long as** itu syarat. Inferensi yang bener biasanya ngikutin syarat itu.
questions.tip_en: **as long as** sets a condition. The right inference usually follows it.

questions.prompt: All of the following are mentioned in the passage EXCEPT
options: easy behaviors became automatic sooner than demanding ones
linking a new behavior to an existing routine can help
volunteers were paid for each day they completed the behavior
questions.evidence_quote: Each day, the volunteers reported whether they had performed the behavior and how automatic it felt.
questions.why_correct_id: Centang yang disebut: kebiasaan gampang lebih cepat otomatis di paragraf 3, ngaitin ke rutinitas lama di paragraf 5, dan tahun 2009 di paragraf 2. Bayaran buat relawan nggak pernah disebut. Itu pengecualiannya.
questions.why_correct_en: Tick what's there: easy behaviors faster (paragraph 3), linking to a routine (paragraph 5), 2009 (paragraph 2). Payment is never mentioned.

why_wrong_id.0: Disebut di paragraf 3: kebiasaan gampang lebih cepat otomatis.
why_wrong_id.1: Disebut di paragraf 5: rencana yang dikaitin ke rutinitas lama.
why_wrong_id.2: Disebut di paragraf 2: **published in 2009**.

why_wrong_en.0: In paragraph 3: easy behaviors became automatic sooner.
why_wrong_en.1: In paragraph 5: linking to an existing routine.
why_wrong_en.2: In paragraph 2: **published in 2009**.

questions.analogy_id: Opsi bayaran itu kayak tamu yang nyelip di foto keluarga. Kelihatan masuk akal, tapi nggak ada di daftar undangan.
questions.analogy_en: The payment option is a stranger in a family photo. Plausible, but not on the guest list.
questions.tip_id: Soal EXCEPT di teks panjang? Cek tiap opsi ke paragrafnya masing-masing, coret yang ketemu.
questions.tip_en: EXCEPT in a long text? Check each option against its paragraph and cross out what you find.

items.title: Forests Between Land and Sea
items.body:
Along many tropical coastlines, a strange kind of forest grows where the land meets the sea. Mangroves are trees and shrubs that can survive in salty water, in mud that is flooded by the tide twice a day. Few other trees could live in such conditions, yet mangrove forests cover large stretches of coast in Asia, Africa, and the Americas. Indonesia alone is home to roughly a fifth of the world's mangroves.

Mangroves have developed several ways to deal with salt and mud. Some species filter most of the salt out at their roots, while others push extra salt out through their leaves. Because the mud contains little oxygen, many mangroves grow special roots that rise above the surface like small pencils, allowing the trees to take in air even when the ground is flooded.

These forests do far more than survive. Their tangled roots slow down waves and hold sediment in place, which reduces coastal erosion. During storms, a wide belt of mangroves can weaken waves before they reach villages, roads, and fields. The roots also create sheltered spaces where young fish, crabs, and shrimp can grow, so many coastal fishing communities depend on healthy mangroves for their income.

Mangroves are also remarkable stores of carbon. Much of the carbon they absorb is locked away in the waterlogged soil beneath them, where it can remain for centuries. Studies suggest that, area for area, mangrove forests can store several times more carbon than many forests on dry land. When mangroves are cleared, however, much of this stored carbon is released into the atmosphere.

Despite these benefits, large areas of mangroves have been lost in recent decades. Forests have been cut down to make room for shrimp ponds, farms, and coastal development. Once the trees are gone, the coast often becomes more vulnerable, and the fish that once used the roots as nurseries disappear as well.

Many countries now run projects to restore mangroves, but planting them is not as simple as it sounds. Seedlings planted in the wrong place, for example where the tide is too deep or the water does not flow freely, often die within a few years. Successful projects usually begin by restoring the natural flow of water and then allowing young trees to grow where conditions suit them.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To argue that shrimp farming should be banned
To explain how to plant a mangrove seedling
To describe mangroves, their value, and the challenges in protecting them
To compare mangroves in Asia and Africa
questions.evidence_quote: These forests do far more than survive.
questions.why_correct_id: Teksnya ngegambarin mangrove dan cara bertahannya (paragraf 1 dan 2), manfaatnya (paragraf 3 dan 4), lalu ancaman dan tantangan pemulihannya (paragraf 5 dan 6). Jawaban ini nyakup ketiganya.
questions.why_correct_en: It describes mangroves and how they cope (1 and 2), their value (3 and 4), and the threats and restoration challenges (5 and 6). This answer covers all three.

why_wrong_id.0: Tambak udang cuma salah satu penyebab hilangnya mangrove. Penulis nggak nuntut larangan.
why_wrong_id.1: Cara nanam cuma dibahas sedikit di paragraf terakhir, dan bukan panduan.
why_wrong_id.3: Asia dan Afrika cuma disebut sebagai lokasi, nggak dibandingin.

why_wrong_en.0: Shrimp ponds are one cause of loss. No ban is argued.
why_wrong_en.1: Planting appears briefly at the end and isn't a guide.
why_wrong_en.3: Asia and Africa are only locations, not compared.

questions.analogy_id: Teks informatif panjang itu kayak dokumenter alam: kenalan sama tokohnya, lihat kehebatannya, lalu lihat ancamannya.
questions.analogy_en: A long informative text is a nature documentary: meet the star, see its strengths, then the threats.
questions.tip_id: Teks yang ngasih fakta tanpa nyuruh pembaca ngapa-ngapain biasanya tujuannya **to describe** atau **to explain**, bukan **to argue**.
questions.tip_en: A text that informs without urging action usually aims **to describe** or **to explain**, not **to argue**.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, why do many mangroves grow roots that rise above the mud?
options: To take in air when the ground is flooded
To push salt out through their leaves
To grow taller than other trees
questions.evidence_quote: Because the mud contains little oxygen, many mangroves grow special roots that rise above the surface like small pencils, allowing the trees to take in air even when the ground is flooded.
questions.why_correct_id: Lumpurnya miskin oksigen, jadi banyak mangrove numbuhin akar yang muncul ke atas permukaan, **allowing the trees to take in air even when the ground is flooded**. Tujuannya biar tetap bisa ambil udara.
questions.why_correct_en: The mud has little oxygen, so these roots rise up, **allowing the trees to take in air even when the ground is flooded**.

why_wrong_id.1: Akar nggak nangkap ikan. Akar jadi tempat berlindung ikan kecil, di paragraf 3.
why_wrong_id.2: Ngeluarin garam lewat daun itu cara lain, bukan fungsi akar ini.
why_wrong_id.3: Tinggi pohon nggak dibahas.

why_wrong_en.1: Roots don't catch fish. They shelter young fish, in paragraph 3.
why_wrong_en.2: Pushing salt out through leaves is a different method, not this root's job.
why_wrong_en.3: Tree height isn't discussed.

questions.analogy_id: Akar napas itu kayak snorkel. Badannya terendam, tapi selangnya nyembul buat ambil udara.
questions.analogy_en: These roots are like a snorkel. The body is underwater, but the tube pokes up for air.
questions.tip_id: **allowing …** di ujung kalimat sering nyebut tujuan atau akibat. Itu jawaban soal **why**.
questions.tip_en: **allowing …** at the end often gives the purpose. That answers **why**.

questions.prompt: The word **their** in paragraph 3 refers to
questions.evidence_quote: Their tangled roots slow down waves and hold sediment in place, which reduces coastal erosion.
questions.why_correct_id: **Their tangled roots**, akar kusut punya siapa? Kalimat sebelumnya bahas **These forests**, hutan mangrove. Akar yang nahan ombak itu akar mangrove.
questions.why_correct_en: **Their tangled roots**, whose roots? The previous sentence is about **These forests**, the mangroves.

why_wrong_id.0: Desa cuma disebut sebagai yang dilindungi dari ombak, dan desa nggak punya akar.
why_wrong_id.1: Ikan kecil berlindung di akar, bukan pemilik akar.
why_wrong_id.3: Ombak itu yang diperlambat akar, bukan pemiliknya.

why_wrong_en.0: Villages are only what the mangroves protect, and villages have no roots.
why_wrong_en.1: Young fish shelter among the roots; they don't own them.
why_wrong_en.3: Waves are slowed by the roots, not their owner.

questions.analogy_id: **Their** itu label nama di tas. Akar cuma mungkin punya pohon.
questions.analogy_en: **Their** is a name tag. Roots can only belong to trees.
questions.tip_id: Pronoun kepemilikan di awal kalimat biasanya nunjuk ke pelaku kalimat sebelumnya.
questions.tip_en: A possessive at the start of a sentence usually points to the previous sentence's subject.

questions.prompt: The word **vulnerable** in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: Once the trees are gone, the coast often becomes more vulnerable, and the fish that once used the roots as nurseries disappear as well.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 3 bilang mangrove ngelindungin pantai dari ombak dan erosi. Kalau pohonnya hilang, pantainya jadi lebih **vulnerable**, gampang kena kerusakan. Jadi artinya **exposed to damage**.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 3 says mangroves protect the coast. Without them, the coast is more **vulnerable**, **exposed to damage**.

why_wrong_id.1: **crowded** (padat) nggak nyambung sama hilangnya pelindung pantai.
why_wrong_id.2: **well protected** malah kebalikannya.
why_wrong_id.3: **wealthy** (kaya) nggak nyambung.

why_wrong_en.1: **crowded** doesn't fit losing protection.
why_wrong_en.2: **well protected** is the opposite.
why_wrong_en.3: **wealthy** doesn't fit.

questions.analogy_id: Pantai tanpa mangrove itu kayak halaman tanpa pagar. Gampang kena apa aja dari luar.
questions.analogy_en: A coast without mangroves is a yard without a fence. Open to anything from outside.
questions.tip_id: Hubungin kata yang ditanya sama paragraf sebelumnya. Hilangnya pelindung berarti makin rentan.
questions.tip_en: Link the word to the earlier paragraph. Losing protection means more exposure.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from paragraph 6 about mangrove restoration?
options: Planting more seedlings always guarantees success.
Projects work best when water conditions are considered first.
Mangroves can only be restored in Indonesia.
questions.evidence_quote: Successful projects usually begin by restoring the natural flow of water and then allowing young trees to grow where conditions suit them.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 6 bilang bibit yang ditanam di tempat yang salah sering mati, dan proyek yang berhasil biasanya mulai dengan ngebalikin aliran air alami. Jadi proyek paling berhasil kalau kondisi airnya diperhatiin duluan.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 6: seedlings in the wrong place often die, and successful projects start by restoring water flow. So projects work best when water comes first.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Banyak bibit yang ditanam di tempat salah malah mati.
why_wrong_id.2: Indonesia cuma disebut di paragraf 1 sebagai tempat mangrove yang luas.
why_wrong_id.3: Teks bilang banyak negara justru lagi ngejalanin proyek pemulihan.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. Seedlings in the wrong place often die.
why_wrong_en.2: Indonesia appears in paragraph 1 only as a large mangrove area.
why_wrong_en.3: Many countries are running restoration projects now.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak nanam bunga di pot tanpa lubang air. Sebanyak apa pun bibitnya, akarnya busuk kalau airnya nggak ngalir.
questions.analogy_en: Like planting flowers in a pot with no drainage. However many seeds, the roots rot if water can't flow.
questions.tip_id: Opsi dengan **always**, **only**, atau **no longer** sering kelebihan klaim di soal inferensi.
questions.tip_en: Options with **always**, **only**, or **no longer** often overclaim in inference questions.
